source_excerpts.title: Degree-fall persistence separates Hilbert behavior from solving cost
source_excerpts.mechanism: A low-degree polynomial may belong to the ideal yet require higher-degree combinations of the chosen generators before becoming available. Track each certified consequence by its actual degree and minimum derivation degree. This supplies a persistence interval measuring a computation obstruction rather than just final ideal membership. The relation between last fall degree and degree-compatible solving degree is a source-backed structural anchor, but extracting a compact complete set of intervals is unproved. Boolean descended systems and direct prime-field systems remain distinct families, with separate nulls and labels.
